key_insight: An explainable machine learning approach using routine, low-cost clinical data can help distinguish Alzheimer’s disease from other causes of cognitive impairment with high accuracy.
clinical_relevance: This could support faster, more accessible preliminary dementia assessment when specialist access is limited, using information already available in standard clinical workflows.
method: Trained two classifiers: a deep neural network and a Light Gradient Boosting Machine.
Used demographic data, patient history, and automatically acquirable neuropsychological test results.
Evaluated on a large National Alzheimer’s Coordinating Center dataset with 167,364 observations and 1,024 features.
evidence_signal: In the abstract, the deep neural network reached 90% accuracy with ROC-AUC 0.96, and LightGBM also reached 90% accuracy with ROC-AUC 0.97, suggesting performance comparable to clinicians under similar information constraints.
watch_item: Results come from retrospective dataset evaluation, so real-world performance, bias, and integration into clinical practice still need prospective validation.
paper_title: Explainable Machine Learning Models for Alzheimer's Diagnosis Using Routine and Low-Cost Clinical Data
